# ExtremeXOS (EXOS) — GUI / CLI / SNMP Mapping

Per `gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`: the CLI column is the literal, complete command line(s) a human would type and that SignalScope must echo verbatim into the terminal pane when a GUI action fires. Because EXOS has no persistent interface/config sub-mode (see `cli-reference.md`), most rows below are a **single self-contained line** — there is no "enter context" line to prepend, unlike the Cisco/Arista/Huawei/Aruba mapping tables.

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `enable port 1:3` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = up(1)` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7`) | `show ports 1:3 information` (admin/oper state), or `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` GET for a lighter targeted re-query | SNMP path usable as fallback per the unification doc's rule (no live CLI session open); standard-MIB object, expected reliable per baseline in `standard-mibs.md`. |
| Disable port | `disable port 1:3` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = down(2)` | Same as above | |
| Set port description | `configure ports 1:3 description-string "uplink to core-sw1 gi0/24"` | `IF-MIB::ifAlias.<ifIndex> = "<text>"` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18`) | `show ports 1:3 information detail` or targeted `ifAlias` GET | Prefer `description-string` (255 chars) over the shorter `display-string` for anything resembling a free-text description field in the GUI. |
| Add port to VLAN, tagged | `configure vlan accounting add ports 1:3 tagged` | `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts` bitmask update (tagged, not in `dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts`) — **or** Extreme's own `EXTREME-VLAN-MIB::extremeVlanOpaqueTaggedPorts` (`1.3.6.1.4.1.1916.1.2.6.1.1.1`, unconfirmed against primary docs, see `mib-reference.md`) | `show vlan accounting` / `show ports 1:3 vlan` | Two plausible SNMP write paths exist (standard Q-BRIDGE vs. Extreme enterprise); neither confirmed as an EXOS-documented SNMP-write workflow this session — treat as CLI-only until verified against a live device. |
| Add port to VLAN, untagged (access) | `configure vlan accounting add ports 1:4 untagged` | `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` bitmask update, plus `dot1qPvid` set for that port | Same as above | GUI must warn/confirm before this action if the port currently has a different untagged VLAN — EXOS's untagged-membership-is-exclusive rule (see `cli-reference.md`) means this can silently displace existing config depending on `auto-move`. |
| Remove port from VLAN | `configure vlan accounting delete ports 1:3` | Corresponding bitmask-clear on the same objects as above | `show vlan accounting` | |
| Add port to STPD | `configure stpd stpd1 add vlan marketing ports 1:2` (or the combined `configure vlan marketing add ports 1:2 tagged stpd stpd1 emistp` form) | No standard-MIB or confirmed Extreme-enterprise SNMP write path found this session for STPD port membership specifically | `show stpd stpd1 ports` | **CLI-only** per this session's research — do not offer an SNMP fallback for this action without further verification; `BRIDGE-MIB`'s `dot1dStpPortTable` is read-only baseline state, not a documented write path, same caveat as every other vendor's classic STP MIB. |
| Add ports to LACP sharing group | `enable sharing 1:1 grouping 1:1-1:4 algorithm address-based L2 lacp` | No standard-MIB (`IEEE8023-LAG-MIB`/`dot3adAgg*`) write support confirmed for EXOS this session, and no Extreme-enterprise equivalent found | `show ports sharing` / `show lacp` | **CLI-only** — same pattern as every other vendor documented so far (LACP membership is consistently CLI-only across vendors per the architecture doc's general finding). |
| Configure port security (MAC locking) | `configure mac-locking ports 1:3 first-arrival limit-learning 4` + `enable mac-locking port 1:3` (two lines — locking must be enabled globally, per-port, and configured) | No confirmed SNMP write path this session | `show mac-locking ports 1:3` | Multi-line CLI sequence — GUI must emit both lines (and, once per device, `enable mac-locking` globally if not already on) since EXOS splits "configure the limit" from "turn on enforcement" into separate verbs. |
| Save configuration | `save configuration primary` (or `secondary`, matching whichever slot the GUI is targeting) | `EXTREME-SYSTEM-MIB::extremeSaveConfiguration` SET (`1.3.6.1.4.1.1916.1.1.1.3`) — **unconfirmed against Extreme's own primary documentation this session**, sourced from third-party MIB mirror only (see `mib-reference.md`) | `EXTREME-SYSTEM-MIB::extremeSaveStatus` GET, or `show switch` / re-run `save configuration` and check for the "no changes" response | GUI must expose **which config slot** (`primary`/`secondary`/named file) is being saved to — unlike Cisco's single `startup-config` target, this is not a one-button-does-one-thing action on EXOS. Do not rely on the SNMP path for this until `extremeSaveConfiguration`'s existence/semantics are confirmed against a live device or an Extreme-hosted MIB file. |
| Configure SNMP community (read-only) | `configure snmp add community readonly public` | N/A — configuring the SNMP agent's own access control cannot itself be done via SNMP (same chicken-and-egg limitation as every other vendor) | `show snmp community` | CLI/GUI-only action by necessity. |
| Configure SNMP trap receiver | `configure snmp add trapreceiver 10.0.0.5 community public` | N/A, same reason as above | `show snmp trapreceiver` (verify exact show-command name against target release) | |
| Configure SNMPv3 `mib-view` access rule | `configure snmpv3 add mib-view myView subtree 1.3.6.1.2.1.2 type included` (plus the paired `add group`/`add access` lines to actually apply it) | N/A, same reason as above | `show snmpv3 mib-view` / `show snmpv3 access` | Multi-line CLI sequence (user → group → mib-view → access, see `mib-reference.md`) — GUI should present this as a single "SNMPv3 access policy" form but must echo all constituent lines in the terminal, not a synthesized one-liner, per the unification doc's "no templating DSL" principle. |

## Open items for implementation (not resolved by this research pass)

- Whether `EXTREME-VLAN-MIB` or `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` is the more reliable SNMP-write target for VLAN membership on a real EXOS switch — both are plausible per the MIB definitions found, but this needs a live-device test before SignalScope picks one as its SNMP-fallback path.
- Whether `extremeSaveConfiguration` is genuinely SET-able on a stock EXOS SNMP configuration (i.e. whether it requires a specific `mib-view`/`access` grant beyond the default admin view) — flagged as unconfirmed throughout this file and `mib-reference.md`.
